blocks.text:
After breakfast, set off on a six-hour tour devoted to São Paulo’s modern and modernist architecture.

The next stop is Ponte Estaiada, the Octávio Frias Bridge. Continue to the Faculty of Architecture and Urbanism at the University of São Paulo (FAU-USP). You will also see Morumbi Stadium, associated in the source programme with architect Vilanova Artigas.

The route continues through Ibirapuera Park, home to the Ciccillo Matarazzo Pavilion and Oca, associated with the work of Oscar Niemeyer. The itinerary also includes a modern art museum associated with Lina Bo Bardi and Hotel Unique, designed by Ruy Ohtake.

Next, explore Higienópolis, an important area of Brazilian modernism, where buildings are associated with Paulo Mendes da Rocha, Isay Weinfeld, Carlos Bratke and Franz Heep.

The final stop is Copan, one of São Paulo’s most recognisable residential buildings.

Main stops: Higienópolis, FAU-USP, Ibirapuera and Copan. Duration: approximately six hours.

blocks.text:
After breakfast, a private city tour of São Paulo’s most representative landmarks, beginning at Ibirapuera Park, the city’s main green space, with the Obelisk, the Monument to the Flags and works by the architect Oscar Niemeyer, including the Museum of Contemporary Art (MAC) and the Oca. Continue through elegant Jardins, with the distinctive Hotel Unique and the traditional Church of Nossa Senhora do Brasil, to Vila Madalena and the colourful, ever-changing graffiti of Beco do Batman.

Then cross the emblematic Avenida Paulista and the historic centre, with the Copan and Itália buildings, the Anhangabaú Valley, the Municipal Theatre, City Hall, the Pátio do Colégio, São Bento Monastery and the magnificent Metropolitan Cathedral on Praça da Sé.

Duration: approximately four hours.
